slides.title:
Competitor Landscape Update:
JNJ-4804 (Guselkumab + Golimumab)
slides.subtitle:
DUET-UC & DUET-CD — Phase 2b Week 48 Data
Ulcerative Colitis & Crohn's Disease
slides.speakerNotes: This deck summarizes the Phase 2b Week 48 data for JNJ-4804 (JNJ-78934804), a co-antibody combining guselkumab (anti-IL-23) + golimumab (anti-TNFα) in a single SC injection. Data presented as late-breaking abstracts at DDW 2026 (May 2–5, 2026). JNJ-4804 showed superiority vs golimumab and numerical superiority vs guselkumab monotherapy in refractory UC and CD. Phase 3 DUET ENCORE trials planned. Key implications for Lilly IBD pipeline (mirikizumab/Omvoh).

slides.title: Drug Overview: JNJ-4804 (JNJ-78934804)

bullets: Generic: JNJ-4804 | Code: JNJ-78934804
Sponsor: Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)
Modality: Fixed-dose co-antibody (bispecific-like) — single SC injection
Targets: IL-23 (guselkumab/TREMFYA) + TNF-α (golimumab/SIMPONI)
Route: Subcutaneous injection
Rationale: Orthogonal pathway blockade → molecular synergy in IBD
Phase: Phase 2b complete (DUET-UC & DUET-CD); Phase 3 DUET ENCORE planned
First and only fixed-dose co-antibody designed for IBD

slides.speakerNotes:
JNJ-4804 (JNJ-78934804) is a fixed-dose combination of guselkumab (anti-IL-23p19, approved as TREMFYA) and golimumab (anti-TNFα, approved as SIMPONI) delivered as a single SC injection. The concept is 'co-antibody therapy' — simultaneous blockade of two complementary inflammatory pathways (IL-23 and TNF) to achieve molecular synergy.

KEY CONTEXT:
- Builds on VEGA Phase 2a proof-of-concept (UEG Week 2022)
- Guselkumab already approved for UC, CD, psoriasis, PsA
- Golimumab approved for UC, RA, PsA, AS
- Also being studied in PsA (AFFINITY Phase 2a)
- NCT05242484 (DUET-UC), NCT05242471 (DUET-CD)

slides.title: Mechanism of Action & Differentiation

bullets: IL-23 pathway: drives Th17/Th22 cells, mucosal inflammation, fibrosis
TNF-α pathway: drives acute inflammation, immune cell recruitment, tissue damage
Orthogonal mechanisms → complementary rather than redundant blockade
Fixed-dose combination in single injection (not separate administrations)
Hypothesis: patients failing monotherapy may benefit from dual blockade
First co-antibody therapy designed for IBD
Targets the two most validated IBD pathways simultaneously
Single injection simplicity vs combination regimens of separate drugs
Leverages two well-characterized, approved agents (safety track record)
Specifically designed for refractory patients (failed ≥1 advanced therapy)
Phase 3 planned: DUET ENCORE-UC and DUET ENCORE-CD

slides.speakerNotes:
RATIONALE FOR COMBINATION:
IBD involves multiple inflammatory pathways. Many patients lose response to anti-TNF (infliximab, adalimumab, golimumab) or anti-IL-23 (guselkumab, risankizumab, mirikizumab) monotherapy. The VEGA Phase 2a study demonstrated proof of concept that induction with guselkumab + golimumab combination was superior to either alone in UC.

VS LILLY (OMVOH/MIRIKIZUMAB):
- Mirikizumab is anti-IL-23p19 monotherapy (same pathway as guselkumab)
- JNJ-4804 adds TNF blockade ON TOP of IL-23 blockade
- This could position JNJ-4804 as the option after IL-23 monotherapy failure
- However, combination carries additive safety risk (infections, malignancy)

VS VEDOLIZUMAB, UPADACITINIB, OZANIMOD:
- Different MOAs entirely — JNJ-4804 targets upstream cytokines

slides.title: DUET Study Program — Design Overview

bullets: Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind
N=577 enrolled
Population: Mod-severe UC, inadequate response/intolerance to ≥1 systemic therapy
~50% had failed ≥2 therapy classes (highly refractory)
Arms: JNJ-4804 (high/mid/low dose) vs Guselkumab vs Golimumab vs Placebo
Primary: Clinical remission at Wk48
Key secondary: CS-free remission, endoscopic improvement, HREI at Wk48
Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind
N=703 enrolled
Population: Mod-severe CD, inadequate response/intolerance to ≥1 systemic therapy
~50% had failed ≥2 therapy classes (highly refractory)
Arms: JNJ-4804 (high/mid/low dose) vs Guselkumab vs Golimumab vs Placebo
Co-primary: Clinical remission + Endoscopic response at Wk48
Key secondary: Endoscopic remission, deep remission, CS-free remission at Wk48

slides.disclaimer: Source: ClinicalTrials.gov & J&J DDW 2026 press release (May 5, 2026). Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
STUDY DESIGN DETAILS:
- Both studies are dose-ranging Phase 2b with active comparators (not just placebo)
- Unique design: tests combination vs EACH component monotherapy
- This allows direct assessment of combination benefit over single agents
- Highly refractory subpopulation analysis is the key differentiator
- Week 48 primary endpoint (longer than typical induction-only studies)

ENROLLMENT:
- DUET-UC: 577 patients (large for Phase 2b)
- DUET-CD: 703 patients (very large for Phase 2b)
- Total program: N=1,280 — well-powered for signal detection

DEFINITIONS:
- UC clinical remission: SFS=0/1, RBS=0, endoscopy subscore 0/1
- CD clinical remission: CDAI <150
- CD endoscopic response: >50% SES-CD improvement or SES-CD ≤2

Presented at DDW May 2–5, 2026 (Abstracts 1058d & 979f)

slides.title: DUET-CD: Key Efficacy Results at Week 48

sections.header: Overall Population — JNJ-4804 High Dose (vs Comparators)
bullets: Clinical remission (CDAI <150): JNJ-4804 50.8% vs Golimumab 25.4% vs Guselkumab 42.5%
Endoscopic response (>50% SES-CD improvement or ≤2): JNJ-4804 38.1% vs Golimumab 19.8% vs Guselkumab 33.9%
JNJ-4804 doubled golimumab on clinical remission (50.8% vs 25.4%)
JNJ-4804 numerically superior to guselkumab monotherapy (+8.3% clinical remission, +4.2% endoscopic response)
Clinical remission: JNJ-4804 nearly DOUBLE the highest comparator
Endoscopic response: JNJ-4804 >60% higher than highest comparator
Clinically meaningful improvements across ALL endpoints vs monotherapies and placebo
This is the key differentiating finding — combo shines in hardest-to-treat patients
Exact percentages for refractory subpopulation not disclosed in press release

slides.disclaimer: Data represents JNJ-4804 high dose group. Source: J&J DDW 2026 press release. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
DUET-CD KEY RESULTS (Week 48, JNJ-4804 high dose):

OVERALL POPULATION:
- Clinical remission (CDAI <150): 50.8% JNJ-4804 vs 42.5% guselkumab vs 25.4% golimumab
- Endoscopic response: 38.1% JNJ-4804 vs 33.9% guselkumab vs 19.8% golimumab

HIGHLY REFRACTORY (failed ≥2 therapy classes, ~50% of enrolled):
- Clinical remission: nearly 2x the highest comparator
- Endoscopic response: >60% higher than highest comparator
- The exact rates were not disclosed in the press release but will be in the DDW abstract

INTERPRETATION:
- The overall population results show numerical advantage but the combo does NOT double guselkumab (50.8 vs 42.5)
- The REFRACTORY subpopulation is where the combo truly differentiates
- This makes clinical sense: patients who failed multiple MOAs may benefit most from dual pathway blockade
- Golimumab alone performs poorly (25.4%) — consistent with its known modest CD efficacy

KEY QUOTE (Sands): 'Results are particularly promising because they show meaningful clinical and endoscopic improvements in patients who have exhausted existing options.'

PRESENTER: Dr. Bruce E. Sands, Icahn School of Medicine / Mount Sinai

slides.title: DUET-UC: Key Efficacy Results at Week 48

bullets: Clinical remission (modified Mayo): JNJ-4804 41.0% vs Golimumab 11.5% vs Guselkumab 34.0%
JNJ-4804 demonstrated SUPERIOR clinical remission vs golimumab (41.0% vs 11.5%; p met)
JNJ-4804 numerically higher than guselkumab monotherapy (+7.0% absolute difference)
Primary endpoint MET for JNJ-4804 vs golimumab comparison
Clinical remission: JNJ-4804 almost 60% HIGHER than closest comparator
Clinically meaningful improvements across ALL endpoints vs monotherapies and placebo
Key secondary endpoints (CS-free remission, endoscopic improvement, HREI) all positive
The highly refractory population is where combo delivers greatest incremental benefit

slides.disclaimer: Clinical remission defined as SFS 0/1, RBS 0, endoscopy subscore 0/1. Source: J&J DDW 2026. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
DUET-UC KEY RESULTS (Week 48):

OVERALL POPULATION:
- Clinical remission: 41.0% JNJ-4804 vs 34.0% guselkumab vs 11.5% golimumab
- SUPERIORITY demonstrated vs golimumab (primary endpoint MET)
- Numerical superiority vs guselkumab (41.0 vs 34.0, Δ=7.0%)

HIGHLY REFRACTORY (failed ≥2):
- Clinical remission: ~60% higher than closest comparator
- Assumes if guselkumab = closest comparator at ~25% → JNJ-4804 ~40% (estimated)

CONTEXTUAL COMPARISON (other Wk48 UC maintenance data):
- Mirikizumab (LUCENT-2 Wk52): clinical remission 49.9% (responders randomized)
- Upadacitinib (U-ACHIEVE Wk52): clinical remission 42.3% (responders)
- Risankizumab (INSPIRE Wk52): clinical remission 40.2% (responders)
- NOTE: DUET enrolled ALL-COMERS (not re-randomized responders) → rates not directly comparable

DEFINITIONS:
- Clinical remission (UC): SFS=0 or 1, RBS=0, endoscopy subscore 0 or 1 (modified Mayo)

Golimumab 11.5% is strikingly low — reflects that TNF monotherapy performs poorly in refractory UC patients.

PRESENTER: Dr. Maria Abreu, Cedars-Sinai

slides.title: DUET Results Summary — JNJ-4804 vs Monotherapies at Week 48
slides.disclaimer: Data from press release (May 5, 2026). Refractory subgroup exact rates not disclosed. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
SUMMARY TABLE — KEY OBSERVATIONS:

1. COMBO vs GOLIMUMAB: Dramatic superiority in both diseases
   - CD: +25.4% clinical remission, +18.3% endoscopic response
   - UC: +29.5% clinical remission
   - Golimumab alone performs poorly in this refractory population (25.4% CD, 11.5% UC)

2. COMBO vs GUSELKUMAB: Modest numerical advantage in overall population
   - CD: +8.3% clinical remission, +4.2% endoscopic response
   - UC: +7.0% clinical remission
   - The incremental benefit of adding TNF to IL-23 is ~7–8% in overall population

3. REFRACTORY SUBGROUP: This is where combo differentiates dramatically
   - Nearly 2× (CD) and ~60% higher (UC) than best comparator
   - Adding TNF blockade provides much greater benefit when patients are refractory

IMPLICATION: JNJ-4804 is positioned as a rescue therapy for patients who fail IL-23 or TNF monotherapy. The overall population benefit over guselkumab alone is modest (~7%), but the refractory benefit is substantial.

slides.title: Safety Summary — DUET-UC & DUET-CD

bullets: Safety findings 'generally consistent with the known profiles of the component monotherapies'
No new safety signals beyond what is known for guselkumab and golimumab individually
No disproportionate increase in serious infections or malignancies reported
Both guselkumab (TREMFYA) and golimumab (SIMPONI) have well-established safety profiles
Guselkumab (anti-IL-23): infections, hepatic events (UC/CD label), injection site reactions
Golimumab (anti-TNF): serious infections, TB reactivation, malignancy risk, demyelination, heart failure
Combination: theoretical additive immunosuppression risk (dual pathway blockade)
Long-term extension (through 2029) will further characterize combination safety
Full safety data to be presented in DDW abstract and subsequent publications

slides.disclaimer: Detailed safety data pending full publication. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
SAFETY INTERPRETATION:

The press release states safety was 'generally consistent with known profiles' — this is standard language for a positive safety readout. Key considerations:

1. GUSELKUMAB SAFETY (known from TREMFYA label):
   - Most common: URI, headache, injection site reactions, arthralgia, diarrhea
   - IBD-specific: hepatic events (liver enzyme elevations, cholestasis) — in UC/CD label
   - Generally favorable safety vs anti-TNF and JAK inhibitors

2. GOLIMUMAB SAFETY (known from SIMPONI label):
   - Anti-TNF class risks: serious infections, TB, opportunistic infections
   - Malignancy risk (lymphoma, skin cancer)
   - Demyelinating disorders, heart failure exacerbation
   - Historically well-tolerated in UC (PURSUIT program)

3. COMBINATION RISK:
   - Dual immunosuppression concern → theoretical increased infection risk
   - HOWEVER: VEGA Phase 2a showed acceptable safety
   - Long-term extension data will be critical for Phase 3 decisions

4. VS LILLY POSITIONING:
   - Mirikizumab (Omvoh) has very clean safety profile (IL-23 monotherapy)
   - JNJ-4804's additive TNF risk may be a differentiating safety concern
   - This could be a Lilly talking point: 'clean IL-23 monotherapy vs combination immunosuppression'

slides.title: Context: VEGA Phase 2a Foundation

bullets: Presented at UEG Week 2022 (Abstract OP087)
Induction combination (guselkumab + golimumab) followed by guselkumab maintenance
Demonstrated superiority of combo induction over monotherapies in UC
Provided the scientific rationale for the DUET Phase 2b program
Sequential design: combo induction → mono maintenance (unlike DUET's combo throughout)
DUET tests combination therapy throughout (induction + maintenance), not just induction
Larger sample sizes (577 UC + 703 CD vs VEGA's smaller POC)
Includes highly refractory subpopulation (failed ≥2 therapy classes)
Dose-ranging with 3 dose levels (high/mid/low)
Week 48 primary endpoint (long-term assessment)
Active comparators (guselkumab & golimumab alone) — not just placebo

slides.speakerNotes:
VEGA → DUET PROGRESSION:

VEGA (Phase 2a):
- Panés J et al. UEG Week 2022, Abstract OP087
- UC induction only (12 weeks)
- Guselkumab + golimumab combo INDUCTION → guselkumab MONOTHERAPY maintenance
- Showed that combo induction yielded higher rates of clinical response and histo-endoscopic mucosal improvement
- Limitation: only tested combo during induction, not maintenance

DUET (Phase 2b):
- Tests the fixed-dose combination (JNJ-4804) throughout the treatment period
- Fixed-dose single injection (not two separate shots)
- Much larger N, dose-ranging, active-controlled
- Includes the critical refractory subpopulation analysis
- Week 48 → assesses durability, not just early response

IMPLICATION: DUET answers whether SUSTAINED combination therapy adds value over monotherapy. Answer appears to be YES, particularly in refractory patients.

slides.title: Competitive Landscape — UC Advanced Therapies (Maintenance/Wk48+)
slides.disclaimer: *Responder re-randomized maintenance designs (rates apply to induction responders only). †From DUET-UC comparator arm. NOT directly comparable due to different designs. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
CRITICAL CAVEAT — CROSS-TRIAL COMPARISON LIMITATIONS:

DUET-UC used an ALL-COMERS design (all patients treated from baseline → Week 48). Most other UC maintenance trials use a RESPONDER RE-RANDOMIZATION design where only induction responders continue to maintenance.

This means:
- JNJ-4804's 41.0% is an ITT rate from baseline
- Mirikizumab's 49.9% is among INDUCTION RESPONDERS only (selected population)
- Direct comparison would require adjusting for induction response rates

IF we assume ~60% induction response → ITT-equivalent maintenance rate:
- Mirikizumab: ~30% ITT-equivalent (0.60 × 0.499)
- Upadacitinib: ~29% ITT-equivalent
- JNJ-4804: 41.0% ITT (as reported)

This would actually make JNJ-4804's results IMPRESSIVE, but this is speculative arithmetic.

ALSO: DUET population is more refractory (≥1 advanced therapy failure required) vs some registrational trials that included bio-naïve patients.

BOTTOM LINE: Cannot directly rank JNJ-4804 vs approved agents without harmonized analysis. But the signal is strong, especially in the refractory subgroup.

slides.title: Competitive Landscape — CD Advanced Therapies (Maintenance/Wk48+)
slides.disclaimer: *Responder re-randomized designs (not ITT from baseline). †From DUET-CD comparator arm. NOT directly comparable. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
CD LANDSCAPE CONTEXT:

- JNJ-4804 50.8% clinical remission (CDAI <150) is in the same range as risankizumab and upadacitinib
- HOWEVER: same caveat applies — DUET is ITT from baseline, others are responder-rerandomized
- Guselkumab alone in DUET-CD achieved 42.5% — consistent with GALAXI Phase 3 data
- Golimumab alone: 25.4% — confirms TNF monotherapy is suboptimal in refractory CD

VS MIRIKIZUMAB IN CD:
- Lilly's mirikizumab Phase 3 in CD (VIVID-1) is ongoing/recently read out
- If mirikizumab achieves ~45-52% maintenance remission (similar to risankizumab), then JNJ-4804's combo would show ~similar overall but differentiate in refractory subgroup

ENDOSCOPIC RESPONSE:
- 38.1% (JNJ-4804) vs 33.9% (guselkumab) in overall population
- Small increment (+4.2%) over guselkumab alone
- Refractory subgroup showed >60% higher endoscopic response (dramatic)

KEY IMPLICATION: The combination's value proposition is PRIMARILY in the refractory population, not the overall population where incremental benefit over IL-23 monotherapy is modest.

slides.title: JNJ-4804 vs Mirikizumab (Omvoh) — Lilly Positioning

bullets: Dual pathway (IL-23 + TNF) → broader inflammation control
Single injection convenience (fixed-dose combination)
Strong refractory data (nearly 2× best mono in CD)
Backed by two approved, well-characterized molecules
J&J has GI franchise depth (TREMFYA, STELARA legacy)
Phase 3 trials starting (DUET ENCORE)
Already APPROVED for UC (2023); CD approval anticipated
Clean safety profile (IL-23 monotherapy, no TNF risk)
No additive immunosuppression concerns
IV induction → SC maintenance (flexibility)
Strong LUCENT-2 data (49.9% maintenance remission)
Lilly commercial infrastructure established

slides.disclaimer: Cross-trial comparison only; no head-to-head data. Review is required before disclosure.
slides.speakerNotes:
HEAD-TO-HEAD POSITIONING:

JNJ-4804 THREAT TO OMVOH:
1. If patients fail Omvoh (anti-IL-23 mono), JNJ-4804 offers next-step combo
2. JNJ-4804's refractory data positions it as THE rescue therapy
3. Physicians may skip IL-23 mono and go straight to combo in severe patients
4. J&J can position as 'the only therapy that blocks two pathways in one shot'

OMVOH DEFENSES:
1. Already approved and building market share
2. JNJ-4804 Phase 3 + approval = ~3-4 year runway for Omvoh
3. Safety advantage: no TNF-associated risks (infections, malignancy)
4. Most patients respond to IL-23 monotherapy — combo not needed for majority
5. Cost: combo likely more expensive; payers may require mono failure first

LIKELY MARKET SEGMENTATION:
- First-line advanced therapy: IL-23 monotherapy (Omvoh, Tremfya, Skyrizi)
- Second/third-line refractory: JNJ-4804 combo (the 'rescue' position)
- This could actually COMPLEMENT Omvoh if Lilly positions smartly

TIMELINE: Phase 3 DUET ENCORE start → ~3 years to data → approval ~2030

slides.title: Clinical & Strategic Implications

sections.header: What This Means for IBD Treatment
bullets: First demonstration that a fixed-dose co-antibody outperforms individual components in IBD
Validates dual pathway (IL-23 + TNF) synergy hypothesis from VEGA
Greatest benefit in refractory patients (failed ≥2 classes) — addresses critical unmet need
May establish new treatment paradigm: mono failure → combination rescue
Phase 3 DUET ENCORE trials will determine if results hold in registrational setting
MODERATE threat to mirikizumab/Omvoh in the near term (3–4 years to approval)
LOW threat to first-line positioning (most patients don't need combo upfront)
HIGH threat in the refractory segment if confirmed in Phase 3
May position Omvoh as the clean first-line option before combo escalation
Combination approach could trigger broader industry shift toward dual-pathway therapies

slides.speakerNotes:
STRATEGIC ASSESSMENT:

THREAT LEVEL: MODERATE (increasing to HIGH if Phase 3 confirms)

NEAR-TERM (2026–2029):
- Omvoh continues to build UC market share unimpeded
- Mirikizumab CD approval provides additional growth runway
- JNJ-4804 is in Phase 2b → Phase 3; no commercial impact yet

MEDIUM-TERM (2029–2031):
- JNJ-4804 Phase 3 readout expected ~2028-2029
- If positive → regulatory filing → approval ~2030
- Impact on Omvoh depends on label (refractory only? or broad?)

LONG-TERM MARKET DYNAMICS:
- IBD market likely to segment by line of therapy
- First-line biologics: IL-23 mono (Omvoh, Tremfya, Skyrizi), JAK (Rinvoq)
- Refractory rescue: JNJ-4804 combo (if approved)
- This actually creates a clean positioning for Omvoh

RISKS:
- If JNJ-4804 gets broad label (not restricted to refractory), it could compete directly
- If combo becomes first-line in severe patients, it erodes all monotherapy market share
- J&J has massive commercial reach in GI (TREMFYA + STELARA legacy)

OPPORTUNITY:
- Lilly could develop its own combination strategies
- Mirikizumab + vedolizumab? Mirikizumab + JAK? (different combinations)
- Or emphasize safety/convenience advantage of mono for the majority

slides.title: Key Takeaways & Recommended Actions
takeaways: JNJ-4804 (guselkumab + golimumab co-antibody) met primary endpoint in DUET-UC: superior clinical remission vs golimumab (41.0% vs 11.5%) at Week 48
In DUET-CD: JNJ-4804 achieved 50.8% clinical remission and 38.1% endoscopic response — numerically superior to both monotherapies
Greatest differentiation in highly refractory patients (failed ≥2 therapy classes): nearly 2× (CD) and ~60% higher (UC) than best monotherapy comparator
Overall population benefit over guselkumab alone is modest (+7–8% clinical remission) — combo value is primarily in the refractory segment
Safety consistent with known profiles of component therapies; no new signals through Week 48
Phase 3 DUET ENCORE trials (UC + CD) planned — potential approval ~2030; JNJ-4804 also being studied in PsA (AFFINITY)
actions: Monitor DUET ENCORE Phase 3 trial designs and enrollment (initiating soon)
Track DDW 2026 full abstract data (refractory subgroup exact rates, secondary endpoints)
Assess implications for Omvoh positioning: emphasize clean IL-23 monotherapy as first-line before combination escalation
Evaluate Lilly's own combination therapy opportunities in IBD (mirikizumab + partner agent)
Update IBD competitive model with JNJ-4804 timeline: Phase 3 readout ~2028–2029, potential approval ~2030
slides.speakerNotes:
SUMMARY: JNJ-4804 is a credible, differentiated competitor that validates dual-pathway combination therapy in IBD. The key finding is that the combo shines brightest in the REFRACTORY population — patients who have exhausted existing options.

For Lilly/Omvoh, this is NOT an existential threat but a market-shaping event:
1. Omvoh has 3–4 years of uncontested growth in its approved indications
2. The modest overall population benefit (+7%) over IL-23 mono suggests most patients won't need combo
3. The refractory segment is real but relatively small (subset of the total market)
4. Safety of combo (dual immunosuppression) may limit broad adoption

OPEN QUESTIONS:
1. Will Phase 3 confirm the refractory subgroup finding? (Phase 2 subgroups often don't replicate)
2. What will the label look like? Restricted to refractory? Or broad?
3. Will payers require IL-23 mono failure before approving combo?
4. What is the pricing strategy for a combination product?
5. Should Lilly explore its own combination approaches?

Review is required before disclosure.
